database.title: Edge cases
database.blurb: Every construct the sample schema lacks, so the port is exercised on real parser output.

domains.title: Core
domains.blurb: Organisations, and a table the narrative still lists but the schema dropped.

domains.title: Work
domains.blurb: Everything an organisation owns. Each org has exactly one profile; the assertion below deliberately says otherwise.

cardinality.why: the profile is the organisation's public page
widgets are built by one organisation and never shared
an attachment is stored under the organisation that uploaded it
an attachment can illustrate a widget
tickets are raised by an organisation's staff
regions are the organisation's own sales territories
a site is located in exactly one of its organisation's regions
jobs run on behalf of one organisation

columns.name: weight
columns.comment: zero default is omitted from the tree

widget.name: widget
description: Schema-qualified, thirty columns wide, RLS enabled with no policy.

attachment.name: attachment
description: Either/or foreign keys guarded by a CHECK: the exclusive-arc check must stay quiet.
checks: (CAST(widget_id IS NOT NULL AS integer) + CAST(ticket_id IS NOT NULL AS integer)) = 1

ticket.name: ticket
description: Soft delete done right (partial unique), an expression index, CHECKs of every shape.

columns.name: label
columns.check: label IS NULL OR (label <> '' AND NOT label LIKE 'tmp%')

columns.name: assignee
columns.check: CASE WHEN state = 'closed' THEN assignee IS NOT NULL ELSE TRUE END

profile.name: profile
description: One profile per org, enforced by UNIQUE; the narrative wrongly claims many.

region.name: region
description: Composite primary key, multi-column foreign key, and a two-table foreign-key cycle.

scratch.name: scratch
description: Claimed by a tenant-scoped domain, but no org_id and no path to org.

job_state.name: job_state
description: Table-level CHECKs, the only way pg_dump writes them: both enum-ish columns are guarded, so
neither may raise undocumented-enum; the two-column CHECK stays on the table.

columns.name: state
columns.check: state = ANY(ARRAY[CAST('open' AS text), CAST('closed' AS text)])

checks: state = ANY(ARRAY[CAST('open' AS text), CAST('closed' AS text)])

app_config.name: app_config
description: One row, enforced as pg_dump shows it (primary key plus CHECK (id = 1)). Asserted as a
singleton in the narratives; must raise no singleton-table finding, unlike profile.

findings.title: Tenant table without row-level security
findings.detail: `attachment` carries `org_id` but RLS is not enabled, so isolation depends entirely on every query remembering the WHERE clause. One forgotten filter is a cross-tenant leak.
findings.suggestion: Enable RLS and add the standard policy.
findings.fix_sql:
ALTER TABLE attachment ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY attachment_tenant_isolation ON attachment USING (org_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid);

findings.title: Domain lists a table that does not exist
findings.detail: Domain `core` claims `ghost_table` but the schema has no such table — likely a rename that never reached the narratives.
findings.suggestion: Fix or remove the entry.

findings.title: Monetary value stored as float
findings.detail: `fee` is binary floating point. 0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3; sums drift; reconciliation against the ledger will be off by cents.
findings.suggestion: Use NUMERIC(p, s) or integer minor units.
findings.fix_sql: ALTER TABLE org ALTER COLUMN fee TYPE numeric(14,2);

findings.title: Tenant table without row-level security
findings.detail: `region` carries `org_id` but RLS is not enabled, so isolation depends entirely on every query remembering the WHERE clause. One forgotten filter is a cross-tenant leak.
findings.suggestion: Enable RLS and add the standard policy.
findings.fix_sql:

findings.title: Asserted relationship has no foreign key
findings.detail: narratives.json says `org` → `scratch` is 1:1, but there is no FK from the child to the parent. The relationship exists only in application code.
findings.suggestion: Add the FK, or correct the narrative.

findings.title: Tenant-scoped domain but no path to the tenant
findings.detail: `scratch` sits in a tenant-scoped domain yet neither has `org_id` nor references anything that leads to it. Its rows cannot be attributed to a tenant at all.
findings.suggestion: Add `org_id` (NOT NULL, FK) or move the table to a global domain in narratives.json.

findings.title: Asserted natural key is not enforced
findings.detail: `(org_id, region)` is declared to identify a `site` row, but nothing enforces it. Retries, double-submits and webhook redeliveries create duplicates.
findings.suggestion: Add a unique constraint (partial if the table is soft-deleted).
findings.fix_sql: ALTER TABLE site ADD CONSTRAINT site_org_id_region_key UNIQUE (org_id, region);

findings.title: RLS enabled but no policy
findings.detail: With RLS on and no policy, non-owner roles see zero rows — usually discovered in staging as 'the table is empty'.
findings.suggestion: Add a policy.

findings.title: Foreign key without index
findings.detail:
PostgreSQL does not index FK columns automatically. Every DELETE/UPDATE on `org` must scan `attachment` to check the constraint, and every join from the parent side is a sequential scan. The scan cost grows with the child table forever, so this gets worse on its own.

An index is not free. Every write to `attachment` maintains it — insert, update and delete alike — and it takes disk. Weigh that against how often `org` rows are actually deleted or re-keyed — if the answer is never, the scan never happens and the index only costs.
findings.suggestion: Add an index on the FK column(s).
findings.fix_sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_attachment_org_id ON attachment(org_id);

findings.title: Foreign key without index
findings.detail:
PostgreSQL does not index FK columns automatically. Every DELETE/UPDATE on `widget` must scan `attachment` to check the constraint, and every join from the parent side is a sequential scan. The scan cost grows with the child table forever, so this gets worse on its own.

An index is not free. Every write to `attachment` maintains it — insert, update and delete alike — and it takes disk. Weigh that against how often `widget` rows are actually deleted or re-keyed — if the answer is never, the scan never happens and the index only costs.
findings.suggestion: Add a partial index, scoped to the rows that have a value. `widget_id` is nullable, so the NULL rows are not indexed at all and the write cost is a fraction of a full index, while the constraint check still uses it.
findings.fix_sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_attachment_widget_id ON attachment(widget_id) WHERE widget_id IS NOT NULL;

findings.title: Modelled 1:1 but intended 1:N
findings.detail: The narrative expects many `profile` per `org`, but the FK is UNIQUE, so the second child will fail to insert.
findings.suggestion: Drop the unique constraint, or fix the narrative.

findings.title: Foreign-key cycle
findings.detail: region → site → region. Rows must be inserted with a deferred constraint or a NULL-then-update dance; backups/restores and truncation have no valid order; ON DELETE CASCADE can loop.
findings.suggestion: Break the cycle (move one FK to a link table) or mark one FK DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED.

findings.title: Foreign key without index
findings.detail:
PostgreSQL does not index FK columns automatically. Every DELETE/UPDATE on `region` must scan `site` to check the constraint, and every join from the parent side is a sequential scan. The scan cost grows with the child table forever, so this gets worse on its own.

An index is not free. Every write to `site` maintains it — insert, update and delete alike — and it takes disk. Weigh that against how often `region` rows are actually deleted or re-keyed — if the answer is never, the scan never happens and the index only costs.
findings.suggestion: Add an index on the FK column(s).
findings.fix_sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_site_org_id_region ON site(org_id, region);

findings.title: Enum-like column with no CHECK
findings.detail: `state` is a short string that clearly takes a fixed set of values, but the database accepts anything. Typos become new states, and nobody can list the legal values without reading application code. The comment lists `open | closed   (enum-ish, no CHECK)`, i.e. the values are known.
findings.suggestion: Add a CHECK constraint (cheap, easy to evolve) or a lookup table if values need metadata. Avoid native ENUM types unless the set is truly frozen.
findings.fix_sql: ALTER TABLE ticket ADD CONSTRAINT ticket_state_check CHECK (state IN (...));

findings.title: Isolated table
findings.detail: `app_config` references nothing and nothing references it. Either it is a staging/log table (fine, say so), or it is dead, or it is the seed of a second data model growing beside the first.
findings.suggestion: Document its purpose or drop it.

findings.title: Tenant FK relies on the default ON DELETE NO ACTION
findings.detail: Deleting a `org` row will fail while `attachment` rows exist. Fine if tenants are never hard-deleted; a surprise the day offboarding/GDPR erasure is built.
findings.suggestion: State the intent explicitly: CASCADE, RESTRICT, or an offboarding job.

findings.title: Relationship has no narrative
findings.detail: `attachment.ticket_id` → `ticket` is one ticket, many attachment · optional · ON DELETE NO ACTION · not indexed, but narratives.json does not say why the relationship exists, so the docs show the constraint and nothing else.
findings.suggestion: Add a `why` to the `ticket` → `attachment` entry in assertions.cardinality (create the entry if it is missing; `expect` is optional).

findings.title: TIMESTAMP without time zone
findings.detail: `created_at` stores wall-clock time with no zone. It reads back differently depending on the session's TimeZone, and DST transitions produce ambiguous values.
findings.suggestion: Use TIMESTAMPTZ.
findings.fix_sql: ALTER TABLE org ALTER COLUMN created_at TYPE timestamptz;

findings.title: Hub table: referenced by 6 tables
findings.detail: Any change to its key, its delete semantics, or its partitioning touches every dependent. Migrations on hub tables need the longest lock windows and the most careful rollout.
findings.suggestion: Treat schema changes here as breaking changes with a written rollout plan.

findings.title: Single-row configuration table
findings.detail: `profile` is documented as holding exactly one row. Nothing enforces that, and the day a second instance is needed (a second GitHub App, a staging vs prod config) every reader that does `SELECT * ... LIMIT 1` becomes wrong.
findings.suggestion: Either enforce one row (CHECK on a constant column with a UNIQUE) or give it a discriminator now (`provider_id`, `environment`) while there is only one row to backfill.
findings.fix_sql:
ALTER TABLE profile ADD COLUMN singleton boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true CHECK (singleton);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX profile_one_row ON profile(singleton);

findings.title: Nullable foreign key
findings.detail: `region.lead_id` may be NULL, so the relationship to `site` is optional. That is legitimate (e.g. approved_by before approval) but often a modelling shrug: a row with no owner, or two nullable FKs that are secretly an either/or.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the optionality is a domain rule; document it in the column comment.

findings.suggestion: Add a `why` to the `site` → `region` entry in assertions.cardinality (create the entry if it is missing; `expect` is optional).

findings.title: Wide table (30 columns)
findings.detail: Tables this wide usually hide several entities (or a JSON column that wants to be one). Every row update rewrites the whole tuple; TOAST kicks in; indexes bloat.
findings.suggestion: Look for column groups that always change together and split them out.
